title: Combining In-Situ Transport Experiments with Real Space Imaging and Resonant Elastic X-Ray Scattering: Chiral Magnets in a Transmission Electron Microscope
content: Nanoscopic magnetic objects are of steadily increasing interest not only in fundamental research but also due to their potential for applications specifically in the field of data storage and manipulation. Here, chiral magnets offer a particularly rich variety of magnetic textures and phases, part of which are non-trivial and topologically protected, which renders them promising materials candidates for such applications. Understanding the nanoscopic nature of such textures, their generation and stability as well as their impact on the electrical properties of their host materials is thus mandatory for paving the way towards the development of novel functional devices.
